title: Bangladesh Crush Pakistan by 104 Runs in Historic Home Test Victory
excerpt: Nahid Rana takes five wickets and captain Shanto scores a century as Bangladesh win their first-ever home Test against Pakistan
body:
Bangladesh rewrote their cricketing history on Monday, bowling Pakistan out for 163 to seal a commanding 104-run victory in the first Test at the Shere Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur. It is the first time Bangladesh have beaten Pakistan in a home Test — and their third consecutive Test win over the visitors, a streak that would have been unthinkable a decade ago.

**How It Unfolded:** Pakistan had looked comfortable after posting 386 in the first innings, but Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto turned the match with a composed 101 in the second innings before making a bold declaration at 240-9, setting Pakistan a target of 268. The gamble paid off spectacularly. Seamer Nahid Rana, just 22, ripped through Pakistan's top order with figures of 5-40, his hostile pace proving too much for a batting lineup that included Shaheen Shah Afridi and Mohammad Rizwan.

**The Bigger Picture:** The result has immediate consequences for the ICC World Test Championship standings. Bangladesh climbed to sixth, while Pakistan slipped to seventh — a grim position for a side that once dominated subcontinental cricket. India, benefiting from the reshuffle, moved up to fifth. For Pakistan captain Pat Cummins and his squad, the defeat exposes familiar frailties: an over-reliance on a few senior batsmen and a fragile middle order that crumbles under sustained pressure.

Shanto's captaincy drew particular praise. *"The declaration was a massive decision,"* he said after the match. *"We backed our bowlers and they delivered."* The boldness reflects a new confidence in Bangladeshi cricket, one that has been building since their 2-0 series sweep of Pakistan in 2024.

For the millions of Bangladeshi-Americans and the broader South Asian diaspora that follows subcontinental cricket religiously, the result is more than a scorecard — it signals a genuine power shift in Asian Test cricket. The rivalry between Bangladesh and Pakistan carries deep cultural weight in diaspora communities from Jackson Heights to Banglatown, where cricket watch parties are weekend fixtures.

**What to Watch:** The second Test begins in Sylhet later this week, where Pakistan will need to win to square the series and salvage their WTC campaign. Bangladesh, riding a wave of momentum, will look to make history again.
